meta.description: Final review: PR-B console navigation branch

user.t:
You are a Senior Code Reviewer with expertise in software architecture, design patterns, and best practices. Your job is to review completed work against its plan or requirements and identify issues before they cascade.

## What Was Implemented
PR-B "Easier navigation" for the ruflo-console Claude Code plugin (TypeScript function-hooks mod, plugins/ruflo-console), 11 commits on branch feat/console-nav in worktree C:\Users\mariu\ruflo-wt-console-nav (base = upstream/main c252cb676; this branch does NOT contain PR-A's Windows fixes):
B1 history trail with agent-aware entries (hooks/history.ts); B2 a mouse "◂ Back" breadcrumb button (the plan's Backspace/Esc items were ruled impossible: pane hotkeys accept one digit/lowercase letter only, and ui.close cannot tell Esc from the close mark); B3 y/n always answer the confirm card (page body drawn through withoutAnswerKeys while an ask is pending); B4 key hints from one table (keyLabel); B5 one group scheme (NAV_GROUPS), one label per page ("Neural Lab", "Claims", "Plugins"…), retired-name aliases, verbs-win parsing; B6 /ruflo go, label prefix/word matching, pages in palette; B7 instant refresh (boot replay moved to Settings), narrow panes keep every shortcut, flat tab bar deleted.

## Requirements / Plan
Plan: C:\Users\mariu\ruflo\docs\superpowers\plans\2026-10-10-ruflo-console-windows-nav-chat.md — read the header, Global Constraints, Review Focus (#5 is this branch's) and the PR-B section only.
Ledger with every ruling and every deferred minor from per-task reviews: C:\Users\mariu\ruflo-wt-console-win\.superpowers\sdd\2026-10-10-ruflo-console-windows-nav-chat\progress.md — triage the PR-B "minor (deferred)" and "Ruling:" lines (Task B1..B7 and PR-B entries): must-fix-before-merge vs follow-up, with reason.

## Git Range to Review
Base: c252cb676  Head: 0fac41cdb
Full package (commit list, stat, diff with context, 222 KB) — read it instead of re-deriving: C:\Users\mariu\ruflo-wt-console-nav\.superpowers\sdd\2026-10-10-ruflo-console-windows-nav-chat\review-c252cb676..0fac41cdb.diff
Review in passes and say so.

## The spec is a vision document
For behaviour the plan is silent on, judge by what a reasonable person navigating this console would expect; a spec's silence is not permission.

## Declined to judge
Before your verdict, list every behaviour you considered and set aside as outside the plan, one line each, with the reason.

## Read-Only Review
Do not mutate the working tree, index, HEAD or branches. One focused vitest run is allowed to settle a concrete doubt (from C:\Users\mariu\ruflo-wt-console-nav\plugins\ruflo-console: `node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run tests/<file>.spec.ts -t "<name>"`). Known environment-only failures on this Windows checkout: specs needing sibling plugins / v3 docs (sparse checkout), symlink EPERM, Windows file modes, Windows path bugs (fixed on the separate PR-A branch), `claude-code/testing` not importable under vitest (all *.test.ts), and events-sweep hotkey tests timing out under full-suite load (pass alone). `claude plugin validate plugins/ruflo-console` passes at head.

## You Do Not Dispatch Subagents

## What to Check
Plan alignment (B1–B7 present; the B2 ruling's substitution is acceptable); cross-task consistency (history/back + Back button + agent drill + key-shadow + narrow hidden keys + group/label renames + viewOf widening + /ruflo go + VERBS all agree — e.g. does a renamed label break a saved trail entry, does the narrow hidden-keys box respect withoutAnswerKeys, does the palette's page rows use canonical labels, do help texts describe the final behaviour); regressions in commands a person or Claude (model tools console_open/console_run) relies on; tests verify real behaviour; PR readiness (CHANGELOG/version per ADR-478 are NOT yet done — the controller adds them at PR time; do not flag their absence).

## Output Format
### Strengths
### Issues (#### Critical / #### Important / #### Minor — each with file:line, what's wrong, why it matters, how to fix)
### Deferred-minor triage (one line per PR-B ledger item: must-fix-before-merge | follow-up, with reason)
### Declined to judge
### Recommendations
### Assessment — **Ready to merge?** Yes | No | With fixes; **Reasoning:** 1-2 sentences.

handback.t:
I reviewed PR-B (c252cb676..0fac41cdb) in four passes: the commit list and stat, the source diff, the tests, then targeted greps on disk at head. I also ran the 8 new specs once: 132 of 132 passed.

### Strengths
- **The trail model is sound** (`hooks/history.ts`). Each entry keeps the agent id, stale entries are skipped without being lost, the cap of 20 is applied, and `replace` keeps Back from pushing the page it leaves. All the old `state.back` readers (help, persist, accent, nav, tabs, cards) now go through one `originOf`. Review Focus #5 is covered in `tests/history.spec.ts`: a vanished agent is matched by id, a missing page id is skipped, and an empty trail falls back to the menu or Overview.
- **The B2 substitution is acceptable.** The Back button reuses the same `back` action, has no hotkey, and leaves the close path alone; `back-button.spec.ts` pins all of this.
- **B3 has one mechanism and checks every page.** `withoutAnswerKeys` is applied to the page body and to the narrow hidden-keys box. `key-shadow.spec.ts` covers all views, with and without an owning page. The only other y/n hotkey in the code is Timeline's `tl-fwd` (checked by grep).
- **B5 makes `NAV_GROUPS` the real source.** The menu's `GROUPS`, `HELP_GROUPS` and the accents are all derived from it. `MENU_SECTIONS` can never hide a page, and the tests enforce the membership.
- **B6 matching is ranked and documented.** A single letter only ever matches a page key. "Verbs win" is protected by a drift test (`VERBS` must equal the switch cases), and the model tool `console_open` still matches exact ids, so it is unaffected.
- **B7 removed the flat tab bar correctly.** It really was unreachable (`hasCards` is `columns >= 44`, the same threshold as `NARROW`). The nav-style setting was rightly kept, because `views/nav.ts:50` still uses it.

### Issues

#### Critical
None.

#### Important
1. **The breadcrumb tells people to press a key that opens a different page.**
   - **Where:** `hooks/views/pane.ts:151-153`. On every page except the agent page, the text says `· b <- <previous page>` whenever the trail has an entry.
   - **What's wrong:** under the B2 ruling there is no global Back key. Outside the agent page, `b` is the Hive-Mind key, and Hive is in `CORE_TABS`, so `b` works from every page. Someone on Claims who reads "b <- Overview" and presses `b` lands on Hive-Mind.
   - **Why it matters:** this is exactly the "help texts describe the final behaviour" check, and it fails. The ledger files it as "redundant"; it is actually wrong.
   - **Fix:** drop `backTo` from the text on non-agent pages; the "◂ Back to X" button already names the page. Keep "b goes back to …" on the agent page, where it is true. Add an assertion in `back-button.spec.ts` that the blurb never contains `b <-` off the agent page.
2. **The Terminal help guide still teaches keys the terminal does not have.**
   - **Where:** `hooks/help-topics-core.ts:218`: "Tab to s stops, o opens a new one, z clears."
   - **What's wrong:** B4 removed this same claim from `HELP` (`commands.ts:163`) and from `harness.ts`. The Stop, New session and Clear buttons have no hotkeys; `views/terminal.ts` gives hotkeys only to the harness picks.
   - **Why it matters:** the "terminal messages" test in `key-labels.spec.ts` only scans `harness.ts`, `views/terminal.ts
[...]
ss `/[.*+?^${}()|[]\]/` is also malformed and escapes nothing.
   - **Why it matters:** it only works because none of the current names contain regex characters.
   - **Fix:** use `String.raw` and the escape helper from `key-labels.spec.ts`.
5. **`/ruflo dump` reads only one word, unlike `go` and `open`.**
   - **Where:** `hooks/commands.ts:115`, which calls `viewOf(second)`.
   - **What's wrong:** `/ruflo dump learning lab` dumps the Learning page, while `/ruflo learning lab` and `/ruflo go learning lab` open the Neural Lab.
   - **Fix:** use `viewOf(rest)` after the verb.
6. **The narrow-pane spec claims more than it tests.**
   - **Where:** `tests/refresh-instant.spec.ts`; the header says "every page key".
   - **What's wrong:** it only asserts the digit keys. At narrow width the letter keys follow the same rule as the wide nav (digit keys, `CORE_TABS` pages and the open page), which is correct but not what the header says.
   - **Fix:** make the header and the commit/PR wording match.

### Deferred-minor triage
**B1**
- Back from a restored or initial page is untested → follow-up: the trail is in memory by design, so a restored page falls back to the menu or Overview.
- The field is named `trail`, not `history` → follow-up: naming only.
- j/k browsing on the agent page does not push history → follow-up: Back still lands on a sensible page.
- `TrailEntry` is written out inline in `state.ts` → follow-up: type hygiene only.
- The agent-page breadcrumb shows the origin page's label when the previous entry is another agent → follow-up: rare, and the label is only slightly off.

**B2**
- The wide blurb's clip width ignores the button width → follow-up: cosmetic, and the text truncates anyway.
- The button is dropped when the view is undefined → follow-up: this cannot happen with real view ids.
- "· b <- X" next to the button → **must-fix-before-merge**: it is not just redundant, it names the Hive-Mind key (Important #1).

**B3**
- Esc is not asserted → follow-up: the host handles Esc, which is out of scope under the ruling.
- Buttons are exempted by key (`confirm`/`cancel`), not by where they come from → follow-up: I checked that no other button uses those keys with y or n.
- The `anyAct` proxy in `key-shadow.spec.ts` is lenient → follow-up: test robustness only.

**B4**
- The scanner misses the "Label (key k)" form → follow-up: no current hint uses it.
- The guard against finding zero hints is weak → follow-up.
- Rare false-positive patterns → follow-up.
- Button wording could be simpler → follow-up.

**B5 (first round)**
- `README.md:54` "The Room" → **must-fix-before-merge**: a one-line fix, and it breaks B5's "one label everywhere" acceptance in user-facing docs (Minor #3).
- `help-topics-more.ts:91` 'Open The Room' → **must-fix-before-merge**: it is a visible button label, same reason.
- `wf-wire.spec.ts:111` has a stale test title → follow-up.
- Code comments still say Learning Lab / Memory Lab → follow-up: comments only.
- The nav search lost its "lab" keywords → follow-up: `/ruflo go` and the palette still find those pages.
- Vacuous assertions at `views.test.ts:1549` and `nav.test.ts:59` → follow-up.
- Terse menu group titles → follow-up: already accepted.

**B5 (second round)**
- The help-lines test in `commands-verbs.spec.ts` is nearly vacuous → follow-up.
- The documented forms `swarm pane|status|claims|consensus`, `agent <id>` and `events/timeline <args>` are untested → follow-up: structurally safe because these verbs are matched before page names.
- `VERBS` is hand-written, with a drift guard → follow-up: the guard is enough.

**B6**
- The "no page called …" wording for ambiguous names → follow-up.
- Words from retired names leak into word matching (`go agent` opens Timeline, `the` opens Room) → follow-up: surprising but harmless and reversible. Recommended fix: keep retired names as whole-name matches only.
- The typed side is not split into words the way page names are (`what's new` with a straight apostrophe fails) → follow-up: the reply lists the close pages, so it is recoverable; a one-line fix.
- The `/ruflo go catalog` footer also shows on filtered command lists → follow-up.
- The palette's +100 boost applies to one-letter queries → follow-up.

**B7**
- `boot-cyber.spec.ts:105` has a stale test title → follow-up.
- Refresh feedback relies on `isRefreshing`/status (no boot flash) → follow-up: by design.
- `pane.ts:267` uses an `as never` cast → follow-up.

### Declined to judge
- **Letter page keys (u f a l v t d m s) don't work from other pages, wide or narrow:** pre-existing. The `isTab`/`CORE_TABS` rule is unchanged from c252cb676; the narrow box now matches the wide nav.
- **The "Letters reach the rest" keys guide and "m plugin catalog" in `HELP`:** pre-existing wording, and the plan doesn't touch it.
- **Esc and close-mark behaviour:** out of scope under the B2 ruling.
- **Back history doesn't survive a reload:** the plan is silent; the trail is in memory and a restored page falls back sensibly.
- **`console_open` (Claude driving the console) adds trail entries:** a reasonable consequence, and the plan is silent.
- **`console_state` titles the agent page "agent":** pre-existing, in `model-tools.ts:214`.
- **On the agent page, Hive's `b` vs. the agent Back button's `b`:** pre-existing; the agent button wins by draw order.
- **Windows path behaviour:** that belongs to PR-A.
- **CHANGELOG and version bump:** the controller adds these at PR time.
- **Menu sub-section names and splits:** accepted in the ledger.

### Recommendations
- Fix Important #1 and #2 and the three "The Room" strings in one small commit, and extend the two scans (help topics text in the terminal-keys check; "The Room" in the retired list) so they can't come back.
- While there: make `dump` use the full rest of the line, and fix the regex in `group-scheme.spec.ts`.
- The plan's manual check ("menu → swarm → agent → Backspace ×2 → overview") can't be run now that Backspace is ruled out. Restate it in the PR body: menu → swarm → agent → Back button ×2 lands on the menu, checked at 40 and 160 columns.
- Follow-up PR: keep retired names as whole-name matches only, and split typed names into words the same way page names are (this fixes `what's new`).

### Assessment
**Ready to merge?** With fixes

**Reasoning:** B1–B7 are all present (B2 per its ruling), consistent across the trail, the Back button, the confirm-key handling, the narrow pane, the renames and `/ruflo go`, and well tested. The blockers are two help texts that send people to the wrong key (the `b <-` breadcrumb and the terminal guide), plus three leftover "The Room" strings — small text fixes.
